$comment: This file is the authored source and is not generated. scripts/build-tokens.mts reads this file and emits app/tokens.generated.css and lib/generated/tokens.ts.

cssNaming.$comment: The ladder is derived from a single `--opsin-radius-base`, so a consuming product changes one value and the whole system re-proportions. The derived values are emitted as literals as well, for consumers that cannot rely on calc() in every context.

rules: One radius decision, then a derived ladder. A product sets `--opsin-radius-base` and nothing else; every other radius is a documented multiple of it.
Radius scales with the box, not with the brand. A 16px chip and a full-screen sheet do not share a radius, because equal radii on unequal boxes look unequal.

Nested corners are concentric: an inner radius is the outer radius minus the padding between them, floored at `radius-xs`. A card with a 20px radius and 16px of padding holds an image at 4px, not at 20px.
`corner-shape` is a progressive enhancement and never a requirement. Everything must be legible and correctly proportioned with plain rounded corners.

base.name: radius-base
base.$comment: 14px, not the 8px web default and not the 0px of the lyra docs chrome. The product theme is squircle and generous; see /docs/theming/lyra-and-the-docs-chrome for why the documentation you are reading looks nothing like it.

ladder.name: radius-none
ladder.use: Full-bleed media and anything that meets a screen edge.

ladder.name: radius-xs
ladder.use: The floor for a nested corner. Tags inside a chip, a swatch inside a legend.

ladder.name: radius-sm
ladder.use: Inputs and small controls inside a card.

ladder.name: radius-lg
ladder.use: Cards on a phone, where the card is nearly the width of the screen.

ladder.name: radius-xl
ladder.use: Sheets and dialogs. Applied to the leading edge only when the surface meets a screen edge on the other side.

ladder.name: radius-full
ladder.use: Pills and circular controls: a status pill, a dial track, an avatar. A pill is a shape and not a size, so it is not a value on the ladder.

cornerShape.$comment: superellipse(4) is a squircle in the Apple sense: the curvature is continuous into the straight edge instead of meeting it at a discontinuity, which is what makes a rounded rectangle look intentional at a large radius. Browsers without `corner-shape` fall back to `round`, which is why every radius above is chosen to look correct as a plain rounded corner first. Support is reported per feature on /docs/start/browser-support and rendered by <BrowserSupport>.
cornerShape.doesNotApplyToNote: Anything using radius-full is already a circle or a pill; a superellipse of a pill is a slightly wrong pill.

hairline.use: Every boundary in the system by default.

emphasis.use: The boundary of a surface carrying `attention` or `urgent`, where the boundary is one of the three non-colour carriers of the status.

focus.use: The focus ring. Always 2px with a 2px offset, always in a colour measured against both the surface and the page behind it, and never removed. See /docs/accessibility/keyboard-and-focus.

inner.name: radius-inner-card
inner.use: A box inside a card at the comfortable density (card padding p-5).

inner.name: radius-inner-card-compact
inner.use: A box inside a card at the compact density (card padding p-4).

concentricity.$comment: The single most common shape defect in a health card is a full-width chart or image with the card's own radius applied to it, which reads as a sticker rather than as part of the card. The `concentricity.inner` array below is the authored pairing set: each entry names an outer ladder step and the padding that sits inside it. Once callout-03.c teaches `build-tokens.mts` to read this array, one `--opsin-radius-inner-{name}` token is emitted per entry, so a component references the concentric radius through that token rather than recomputing it. Until the token exists, or for a consumer that has not regenerated, apply the value directly, computing it by hand from the two tokens involved as the inline style value `max(calc(var(--opsin-radius-{outer}) - var(--opsin-space-{pad})), var(--opsin-radius-xs))`, which is floored at `--opsin-radius-xs`. Only the two pairings the system actually ships are listed: a box inside a card at the comfortable density and a box inside a card at the compact density. A ladder step nobody pairs with a published padding gets no entry, because a token no component consumes is a token nobody keeps correct.
